findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the end-to-end test to assert scorer outcomes for a FakeRunner whose finding is correctly attributed (e.g. `criteria: ['G3']`), and make `_attributes_criterion` read the `criteria` list so that a correctly attributed container finding passes `attributes_g3_vs_g4`.
evidence: eval_scorers.py:297 `hay = " ".join(str(f.get(k, "")) for k in ("criterion", "dimension", "title", "detail"))`
passes.py:394-412: pass1_container finding keys are finding/criteria/location/evidence/scenarios/impact/checklist_item/suggested_fix/_agentic/_container_child/_container_bin/cohort
plan-review-container.eval.yaml lists `attributes_g3_vs_g4` as a deterministic scorer, and its comment says 'Deterministic scorers GATE the build'
Plan AC 1 only checks `coverage == 1.0`
findings.finding: The plan's only end-to-end check is `coverage == 1.0`. It never checks that the specs' gating deterministic scorers can read the output shape the new arms return. For the container spec they cannot. `attributes_g3_vs_g4` (`_attributes_criterion`) looks for the gold criterion in finding keys `criterion`, `dimension`, `title`, `detail`. `pass1_container` findings carry `criteria` (a list), `finding`, `location` and `evidence`, none of which the scorer reads. Every G3/G4 should-fire case will therefore fail that gating scorer. The fix swaps a run-error failure for a scorer-shape failure, and its own tests won't catch it.
findings.location: Testing ('end to end: run_eval … reports coverage == 1.0'); Acceptance Criteria item 1; src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_scorers.py `_attributes_criterion`
scenarios: After the fix, eval-live runs the container spec. Coverage is 1.0, but every G3/G4 recall case fails `attributes_g3_vs_g4` even when the model attributes correctly, so the spec gate fails.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_attributes_criterion`, also match the gold id against each finding's `criteria` list (exact, case-insensitive membership), alongside the existing string keys. Add `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_scorers.py` to Scope and a test that a canned `{'findings':[{'criteria':['G3'], ...}]}` passes for a G3 fire case.

plan-review-container.eval.yaml header and `tolerance` block: the spec exists to compare merged/bin-packed candidate calls with baselines for recall, false-accept and G3/G4 attribution_accuracy_floor 0.90
findings.finding: For `plan-review-container`, the container arm sends each case through `_run_criterion_case`. That calls `pass1_container(criteria=[desc])` with only the case's gold criterion. The production gate makes one merged call over ALL container criteria (G3, G4, decomp-shape). The plan's stated rationale ('the eval scores the same code path the gate runs') therefore does not hold for this spec. With a single-criterion rubric, any finding tagged with the other criterion is dropped, so G3-vs-G4 attribution is right by construction. A G4 false fire on a G3 pass case can never show up either.
findings.location: Approach step 1 (Pass-finder arm, PASS_CONTAINER); src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py `_run_criterion_case` container branch
scenarios: A G3 recall case where the model would wrongly tag the gap as G4 still scores as correctly attributed, because G4 is not in the rubric.
A G4 pass case where the merged production call would false-fire G3 is never detected.
findings.suggested_fix: In the PASS_CONTAINER branch, build `criteria=[registry.by_id(repo_root)[c] for c in CONTAINER_CRITERIA if c in registry.by_id(repo_root)]` and call `passes.pass1_container` directly, with the case's `input` as parent_plan, its `children`, and `case.get('sibling_roster') or build_sibling_roster(children)` as the roster. Use the case's `criterion` only for validation and scoring. Keep `_run_criterion_case` for PASS_FINDER cases.

No criterion shows the new arms working against the real model. The new path calls `pass1_chunk`, `pass1_container` and `pass1_isf` on real structured responses in production, and the offline `FakeRunner` bypasses that parsing.

findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: '[non-codebase] A live eval run (prompt-eval.yml eval-live or equivalent local run) over plan-review-finder, -container and -isf-finder shows 0 "no eval solver" run errors and coverage > 0; run id recorded on the ticket.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether a criterion/spec family mismatch is allowed; if not, raise ValueError when PASS_FINDER receives a container criterion or PASS_CONTAINER receives a non-container one, and add a test.
evidence: 'when prompt_id is passes.PASS_FINDER or passes.PASS_CONTAINER, read the case's criterion ... run _run_criterion_case for it (which already routes container criteria to pass1_container and the rest to pass1_chunk)'
Root cause: 'every container case (G3/G4) carries the children payload' — does not state whether plan-review-finder contains G3/G4 cases
findings.finding: The pass-finder arm routes purely on the case's `criterion` field: `_run_criterion_case` sends container criteria to `pass1_container` and the rest to `pass1_chunk`. The plan never says what happens when a case's criterion family does not match the spec's prompt, for example a G3/G4 case inside plan-review-finder or a non-container criterion inside plan-review-container. In that case the spec silently scores a different PASS prompt than the one it is named for.
scenarios: A finder-spec case with criterion G3 is scored on the container prompt, so plan-review-finder metrics mix two prompts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the exact resolution call for a case's `criterion` value (e.g. `registry.by_id[case['criterion']]` or `_criterion_id(f'plan-review-{criterion}')`).
evidence: '_criterion_id(prompt_id) ... strips plan-review- and looks the remainder up in the criterion registry'
'read the case's criterion, resolve it with _criterion_id'
'every value resolves in registry.by_id (checked: 0 unresolved)'
findings.finding: Step 1 says to resolve the case's `criterion` value (e.g. 'T2') with `_criterion_id`. Per the Root cause, that helper strips a `plan-review-` prefix from a prompt id. The plan does not state whether it is called with the bare value, with a synthesized 'plan-review-<criterion>', or replaced by a direct `registry.by_id` lookup. This matters because the Root cause verified resolution against `registry.by_id`, not via `_criterion_id`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the end-to-end test use the same solve entrypoint that eval-live uses (with FakeRunner injected), or add an AC that a post-merge eval-live run reports non-zero coverage with no 'no eval solver' errors for the three specs.
evidence: "end to end: `run_eval` over each of the three specs with a solve that delegates to `run_case` with a `FakeRunner` reports `coverage == 1.0`"
Problem section: the defect is observed in `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` (`eval-live`), the live path.
findings.finding: The end-to-end acceptance criterion runs run_eval with a solve the test builds ("a solve that delegates to run_case with a FakeRunner"). It does not run the solve or solver wiring that the eval-live job actually uses. The reported symptom is in the live loop, so the AC can go green even if the production solve does not reach the new arms for these specs.
scenarios: The production solve used by eval-live builds its runner or config differently, or filters specs before reaching run_case. The offline AC passes while the live loop still reports 0.00 coverage for one of the three specs.
